text:
sara: Escalation from ACME — their Private/VPC deployment reports TLS handshake failures when our client hits their LB. Customer: "GET https://api.redwood.example -> TLS handshake error". Attached their initial curl output. Can eng help triage? :frowning:

sara: curl output they pasted:
```
curl: (35) error:1409442E:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure
```

sara: They say this started after their infra team swapped the load balancer TLS profile to a corporate standard. No other app is failing in their environment (only our endpoint).

zack: Thanks — can you ask for an `openssl s_client -connect <lb>:443 -servername api.redwood.example -alpn h2` dump (no POST data) and the LB TLS profile (protocols + ciphers)? That error usually means server rejected the client cipher list or signature algs.

sara: Got the s_client from ACME (redacted host):
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
139832...:errno=0
---
no peer certificate available
---
SSL handshake has read 5 bytes and written 290 bytes
---
SSL: error:1417A0C1:SSL routines:tls_process_server_certificate:certificate verify failed
```

sara: Their LB team also sent the TLS profile settings snippet: `protocols: TLSv1.2`, `ciphers: RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384` and explicit disabled curves list (ECDSA removed).

mike: Ok — two signals here: (1) LB is terminating TLS and it's configured to only present RSA-based certs/ciphers or to prefer RSA sigs; (2) our hosted front uses ECDSA leaf certs for SNI-backed routing in that region when certain cert rotation occurs. If the LB has a strict cipher list that excludes ECDSA signature algs or ECDHE-ECDSA ciphers, the LB may drop the backend re-encrypt or refuse to negotiate on ALPN h2 -> handshake fails.

zack: Exactly. Also `no peer certificate available` suggests the LB is acting as a mutating proxy or there's an intermediate rewrite. If the customer LB expects RSA-only chains, and our endpoint advertises an ECDSA cert, the LB might reject it rather than passing through.

sara: They are using "reencrypt" mode (LB re-encrypts to backend) and have a strict corporate cipher order (they shipped profile to prod).

mike: Repro steps for support to confirm (quick):
- Ask ACME to run `openssl s_client -connect <lb>:443 -tls1_2 -ciphers 'ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384' -servername api.redwood.example` and report results.
- From our side, try curl to their LB with `--tlsv1.2 --ciphers` to see if connection succeeds when forcing an ECDSA cipher.

sara: They ran the openssl test and it fails with the ECDSA cipher; works when forcing an RSA cipher.

zack: That confirms LB rejects ECDSA. Two remediation paths:
1) Customer: update LB TLS profile to allow ECDHE-ECDSA ciphers and TLS1.3 (preferred). Example config for F5/NGINX: 
```
ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
ssl_ciphers 'ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:...';
ssl_prefer_server_ciphers on;
```
2) Our side: provide an RSA-signed certificate alternative for the affected endpoint or route customer traffic to a node with RSA chain (short-term mitigation).

mike: Action items:
- sara: ask ACME infra to try enabling TLS1.3 / add ECDHE-ECDSA ciphers. If they can't, request they whitelist our dedicated-IP pool for a bypass to a region where we present RSA certs.
- zack: can we check if any hosts in `prod-eu` currently present RSA chain for the SNI `api.redwood.example`? If yes, we can route ACME there as workaround.
- eng-oncall (cc @zack) to consider adding an automated fallback: if client TLS fails with handshake errors and LB/Proxy SNI shows macroscopic reject patterns, attempt to prefer RSA chain variant for that tenant for next 24–48h while customer remediates.

sara: ACME asked if this is something they changed or we did. I confirmed we recently rotated an ECDSA leaf in that cert family last week — they rolled out a stricter company TLS profile the next day. Timing lines up.

zack: Good to know. If customer policy can't be relaxed due to compliance, we should offer the RSA fallback + documented repro so their security team can sign off.

sara: I'm provisioning the reproduce checklist and will update ACME with the two mitigation options. cc: @mike for the routing check.

deploy-bot: Deployment notice — cert rotation for `edge-cert-2026-03-10` (ECDSA) applied to region `eu-west-1` on 2026-03-10 03:12 UTC.

mike: That deploy-bot note is exactly the rotation. We'll treat this as a customer config incompatibility rather than a platform outage.

sara: Next: I'll open a customer-facing ticket with step-by-step repro, recommended config for their LB, and the temporary routing/RSA fallback option. Also will attach curl/openssl commands.

zack: If you need eng help re-routing or provisioning RSA chain nodes, ping me and I'll coordinate with runtime infra.

sara: thanks all — filing KB draft and routing request now. :thumbsup:
